name: Andrab Lake
summary: Small alpine lake north of Kalam on the OSM map.
access: Hike; summer.

name: Bahrain (Behrain)
summary: Riverside town at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers, with handicraft markets and the trailhead for Daral and Saidgai lakes.

facts.text: The name means 'two rivers' for the Daral/Swat confluence.
facts.quote: due to its location at the confluence of the Daral and Swat rivers

facts.text: It is a base camp for the Daral and Saidgai lakes trail.
facts.quote: It also serves as a base camp for the trail that leads to the Daral and Saidgai lakes.

facts.text: It lies 60 km north of Mingora at 4,700 ft on the right bank of the Swat River.
facts.quote: 60 km north of Mingora at an elevation of 4,700 ft on the right bank of the Swat River

facts.text: It is known for riverside tourist resorts and local handicrafts.
facts.quote: It is known for its riverside tourist resorts, local handicrafts, and its view of the merging of the Daral and Swat rivers.

facts.text: Some houses have carved wooden doors, pillars and balconies.
facts.quote: Some of the houses have carved wooden doors, pillars and balconies.

access: N-95, 60 km north of Mingora; year-round road.

name: Chitral
summary: Chitral town on the Chitral River; pointer only, for the far end of the Lowari road and the Kachi Kani / Ploga links from Swat.

timeline.event: Chitral became the capital of the Kingdom of Chitral under the Katur dynasty.
timeline.quote: From 1571 onwards Chitral was the capital of the Kingdom of Chitral under the rule of the Katūr dynasty.

timeline.event: The British garrison at Chitral Fort was besieged by the Chitralis during the Chitral Expedition.
timeline.quote: The British garrison faced a month-long siege at Chitral Fort by the Chitralis in 1895 during the Chitral Expedition.

facts.text: Town on the Chitral River in northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
facts.quote: is a town situated on the Chitral River in the northern part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan.

facts.text: Chitral is the capital of Lower Chitral district and was earlier capital of Chitral state.
facts.quote: It serves as the capital of the Lower Chitral District, and was previously the capital of Chitral District, and before that, the capital of Chitral State

facts.text: The Kator dynasty made it capital of the kingdom of Chitral from 1571.
facts.quote: From 1571 onwards Chitral was the capital of the Kingdom of Chitral under the rule of the Katūr dynasty.

facts.text: A British garrison endured a month-long siege at Chitral Fort in 1895.
facts.quote: The British garrison faced a month-long siege at Chitral Fort by the Chitralis in 1895 during the Chitral Expedition.

access: N-45 via Lowari Tunnel from Dir.

name: Dir (Dir Khas)
summary: Former capital of Dir state and Upper Dir seat, at the foot of Lowari Pass on the road to Chitral; the road to Kumrat leaves the main road here.

timeline.event: Dir state was fully incorporated into Pakistan.
timeline.quote: It was the capital of the former princely state of Dir, until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.

facts.text: At the base of Lowarai Pass on the road to Chitral.
facts.quote: It is at the base of the Lowarai Pass, the main road to Chitral.

facts.text: Founded in the 17th century.
facts.quote: Dir was founded in the 17th century.

facts.text: Dir was the capital of the princely state of Dir until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.
facts.quote: It was the capital of the former princely state of Dir, until its full incorporation into Pakistan in 1969.

facts.text: The former royal palace stands on a hill above the city.
facts.quote: The former royal palace is on a hill above the city.

facts.text: The town lies along the Dir River, a tributary of the Panjkora.
facts.quote: It lies along the Dir River, a tributary of the Panjkora River.

access: N-45 from Chakdara/Timergara.

name: Fatehpur (Swat)
summary: Union council and small town on the Swat valley road between Madyan and Khwazakhela.

facts.text: Fatehpur is a union council of Upper Swat.
facts.quote: Fatehpur is an administrative unit, known as Union council, of Upper Swat District in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan.

access: On the main Swat valley road (N-95) north of Mingora.

name: Gabral
summary: Gujar-Gawri village where the Gabral River meets the Utror river; gateway to Shahi Bagh, Kharkhari and Mushroom Lake.

facts.text: It stands at 2,286 m on the Gabral River.
facts.quote: Gabral is located at an elevation of 2,286 metres (7,500 ft).

facts.text: The Gabral River joins the Utror River there.
facts.quote: where the Gabral River joins the Utror River, a tributary of the Swat River

facts.text: It is about 7 km from Utror by road and 20 km from Kalam.
facts.quote: It is about 7 kilometres (4.3 mi) northwest (by road) from Utror, 20 kilometres (12 mi) west of Kalam

facts.text: The valley's altitude ranges from 2,580 m at Baila to 5,160 m at Karkaray Lake top.
facts.quote: The altitude of the valley ranges from 2580 m at Baila to 5160 m at Karkaray Lake top.

facts.text: 44 medicinal plants are collected in Utror and Gabral from May to August.
facts.quote: In Utror and Gabral, 44 medicinal plants are collected during the months of May, June, July and August.

access: Jeep road from Utror (~7 km) or Kalam (~20 km).

name: Izmis Lake
summary: Lake above the tree line SW of Utror, ringed by caves.

facts.text: Named after surrounding caves.
facts.quote: as the lake is surrounded by several natural caves, the people have named the lake after these caves

facts.text: A jeep link road leads part of the way from Utror.
facts.quote: A small jeep-able link road from Utror leads part of the way to the lake

facts.text: The lake can be reached after about 3-6 hours of trekking from the end of the jeep road.
facts.quote: The lake can be accessed from here after trekking for almost 3-6 hours.

facts.text: Izmis Lake is harder to enter than Mahodand and Kundol and needs trekking.
facts.quote: Other lakes in the region, such as Izmis Lake, are harder to enter and need to be done so through trekking.

access: Jeep to Loypanghalay, then trek 3-6 h.

summary: Remote lake in the Falak Sar valley below the peak.

facts.text: It is an alpine glacial lake in the Ushu valley of Swat Kohistan.
facts.quote: Jabba Lake, also known as Jaba Lake is an alpine glacial lake located in the Ushu valley of Swat Kohistan region in northern Pakistan.

facts.text: The lake is at about 14,000 ft above sea level.
facts.quote: Elevation of lake is about 14,000 feet above sea level.

access: Trek.

name: Jandrai (Jandarai)
summary: Village on the unpaved jeep road to Jahaz Banda, where the road ends and the trek begins.

facts.text: Jeep road ends at Jandrai; the rest to Jahaz Banda is a trek.
facts.quote: it ascends toward Jandrai village via a passable but unpaved road suitable for jeeps. Beyond this point, the journey transitions to a trek, leading to Jahaz Banda.

facts.text: A passable but unpaved road suitable for jeeps climbs to Jandrai village.
facts.quote: From there, it ascends toward Jandrai village via a passable but unpaved road suitable for jeeps.

access: Jeep from Thal/Kumrat via Darwaza and Lamoti (per Wikipedia), then trek to Jahaz Banda.

name: Kalam
summary: Main tourist base of upper Swat, on a terrace where the Swat River forms from the Gabral (Utror) and Ushu rivers; the road head for Ushu, Matiltan, Mahodand, Utror and Gabral.

timeline.event: Kalam was the centre of an independent state.
timeline.quote: it was the centre of an independent state in the 19th century.

facts.text: The Swat River forms at Kalam from the Gabral and Ushu rivers.
facts.quote: It is the site where the Swat River forms as a result of the confluence of two major tributaries, the Gabral and Ushu rivers.

facts.text: It lies 99 km north of Mingora at about 2,000 m.
facts.quote: Located 99 kilometres (62 mi) north from Mingora and at an elevation of about 2,000 m

facts.text: It is mainly inhabited by Gawri people.
facts.quote: Kalam valley is predominantly inhabited by Gawri people.

facts.text: The metalled road ends here; a shingle road continues to the Ushu and Utror valleys.
facts.quote: here, the metalled road ends and shingle road leads to the Ushu and Utrot valleys.

facts.text: Two notable lakes, Mahodand and Kundol, are frequently visited because of their easy access routes.
facts.quote: Two notable lakes in the Kalam valley are the Mahodand Lake and Kandol Lake, both of which are frequently visited due to their easy access routes.

access: N-95 from Mingora, 99 km (3-4 h); open most of the year, snow in winter.

facts.text: Named for its bowl shape.
facts.quote: It was named after the lake's resemblance to a bowl.

facts.text: The lake sits at 11,500 ft (3,500 m).
facts.quote: surface elevation 11,500 ft (3,500 m)

facts.text: The lake is fed by snowmelt from the surrounding glaciers.
facts.quote: The lake is fed by the snowmelt from the surrounding glaciers.

name: Khwazakhela
summary: Second-largest commercial centre of Swat after Mingora, where shoppers from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla come to trade; junction town for the Shangla road.

timeline.event: The Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque was built near Khwazakhela by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.
timeline.quote: One important historical site in the area is the Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque, which was built in the 12th century by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.

facts.text: Second-largest commercial centre in Swat.
facts.quote: Khwazakhela is the second-largest commercial center in Swat after Mingora.

facts.text: Draws people from Kalam, Kohistan and Shangla.
facts.quote: Many people from Kalam, Kohistan, and Shangla come here for shopping and business.

facts.text: The Lwar-e-Jamat mosque in the area dates to the 12th century.
facts.quote: One important historical site in the area is the Lwar-e-Jamat Mosque, which was built in the 12th century by Mahmud of Ghazni during his visit.

facts.text: It is well known for the graves of religious saints.
facts.quote: Khwazakhela is well known for the graves of religious saints (Awliya).

facts.text: It had a population of 57,113 in the 2023 census.
facts.quote: As of the 2023 census, Khwazakhela had a population of 57,113.

summary: Glacier-fed lake north of Utror reached on foot from Ladu; source of the Utror khwar.

facts.text: Elevation 9,950 ft in the north of Utror.
facts.quote: Kundol Lake lies in the lap of Hindu Kush mountains at an elevation of (9,950 ft), in the north of Utror

facts.text: Only accessible in summer.
facts.quote: Kundol Lake is accessible only during summer.

facts.text: Folktale of a golden bowl.
facts.quote: a golden bowl materializes at its center

facts.text: It is 19 km from Kalam.
facts.quote: It is 19 kilometres (12 mi) away from the Kalam valley.

facts.text: The lake gives rise to the Utror Khwar, a major right tributary of the Swat River.
facts.quote: It gives rise to Utror Khwar, the major right tributary of the Swat River.

summary: Summer hamlet in the Ladu valley above Utror, known for potatoes and turnips; the road head and trailhead for Kundol Lake and Spin Khwar Lake.

facts.quote: You can either hike to Ladu from Utror or take a four-wheeler to ease and minimize your journey. It consumes almost two hours to reach the beautiful valley of Ladu.

facts.text: There is a small hut in Ladu serving tea and food.
facts.quote: There is also a small hut in Ladu where you can take tea and get something for eating.

facts.text: Summer residents plough the land and harvest potatoes and turnips.
facts.quote: The people who take temporary residency over here during summer plow the open land and harvest potatoes and turnips

access: On foot from Laddu village; no mapped path reaches the lake in OSM (see swat_routes.json gap notes).

name: Madyan
summary: Bustling Torwali-majority riverside town where the Chail and Swat valleys join; a dining and shopping stop and base for the Bahrain-Kalam road.

facts.text: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.
facts.quote: Madyan is primarily inhabited by Torwalis.

facts.text: The Chail and Swat valleys join at Madyan.
facts.quote: The two valleys join at Madyan, 8 km below Bahrain.

facts.text: It stands at 1,321 m and has many hotels in all price ranges and some good tourist shopping.
facts.quote: at 1,321 m (4,335 feet) above sea level, but it is a larger town and has many hotels in all price ranges and some good tourist shopping.

facts.text: Shawls, embroidery, tribal jewellery, carved wood and coins are sold along the main street.
facts.quote: Antique and modern shawls, traditional embroidery, tribal jewellery, carved wood and antique or reproduced coins are sold along the main street.

facts.text: The central mosque has carved wooden pillars with elegant scroll capitals.
facts.quote: The central mosque at Madyan has carved wooden pillars with elegant scroll capitals

summary: Large glacial lake at the head of the Ushu valley, reachable by jeep from Kalam in summer and popular for boating and camping.

facts.text: It lies about 40 km from Kalam in the Usho sub-valley.
facts.quote: Mahodand Lake is a large lake in the Swat Valley, located approximately 40 km from Kalam, in the Usho Sub-valley

facts.text: Elevation about 2,865 m.
facts.quote: at an elevation of 2,865 m (9,400 ft)

facts.text: It is reached by four-wheel drive and is a good resort for fishing, boating and camping.
facts.quote: It is accessible with a four-wheel drive vehicle, and is a good resort for fishing, boating and camping.

facts.text: The lake is fed by melting glaciers and springs.
facts.quote: The Mahodand Lake is fed by melting glaciers and springs of the mount Hindu Kush.

facts.text: Its Pashto name means lake of fishes.
facts.quote: lake of fishes

summary: Highest peak of the Swat valley, a 5,918 m Hindu Kush summit.

name: Jamia Masjid Thal (wooden mosque)

Second-floor work began; finished about nine years later

name: Mankial Sar
summary: Second-highest peak of the Swat valley, east of Kalam.
